349.h: Yusuf Maitama Sule University, Kano is a public university owned by the Kano State Government, founded as Northwest University, Kano. Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso inaugurated a planning committee on 24 November 2011 to draw up a blueprint. On 27 March 2012 the National Universities Commission approved the university as Nigeria's 37th state university and 123rd university overall, and the governor set up an implementation committee the same day to appoint staff and admit the first students. It was later renamed after Yusuf Maitama Sule, the Kano-born statesman and diplomat.
349.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
349.c: It is located in Kano and provides hostel accommodation for students.

358.h: The Nigerian Army University, Biu (NAUB) is a federal university established by the Nigerian Army. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2018. It was set up to attract good teaching and research staff and talented students, and to encourage innovation and entrepreneurship.
358.a: The National Universities Commission has approved 31 postgraduate programmes at NAUB, alongside its undergraduate degrees. A Directorate of Basic and Pre-Degree Programmes widens access, and the university has set up a committee to establish a College of Medical Sciences and a university teaching hospital.
358.c: It is located in Biu, Borno State, in north-eastern Nigeria.

363.h: The Federal University of Health Sciences, Azare (FUHSA) was established in 2021 under President Muhammadu Buhari, one of eleven new federal universities created across the six geopolitical zones. It admitted 760 pioneer students in the merged 2021/2022 and 2022/2023 sessions.
363.a: FUHSA is organised into health-focused faculties, including Allied Health Sciences, Basic Clinical Sciences, Basic Medical Sciences, and Medicine and patient care. Together they cover the structure and function of the body, the study of disease and diagnosis, rehabilitation and support, and clinical medicine.
363.c: It is in Azare, the headquarters of Katagum local government area in Bauchi State.

366.h: Admiralty University of Nigeria (ADUN) is owned by the Nigerian Navy through its investment arm, Navy Holdings Limited. It was originally established as a private university, and the National Universities Commission lists it among federal universities from 2023. The university emphasises small classes and an uninterrupted academic calendar, so that students graduate on schedule.
366.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes in engineering, sciences and other fields.
366.c: ADUN has two campuses. The main campus covers 100 hectares on the Ibusa-Ogwashi-Uku expressway, about 20 kilometres from Asaba, Delta State. A second campus of 203 acres is at the Nigerian Navy Engineering College site in Sapele.

367.h: The Federal University of Transportation, Daura (FUTD) is a specialised federal university established in 2022, with a mission of education, research and innovation in transport and port management.
367.a: FUTD offers programmes that prepare professionals for the transport sector. Its civil engineering programme covers structural analysis, geotechnics, hydraulics, construction management and materials, with an emphasis on transport infrastructure, and it also has a Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering.
367.c: It is located in Daura, Katsina State.

368.h: The African Aviation and Aerospace University (AAAU) is a public university founded in 2022 by the Nigerian Government and overseen by the Federal Ministry of Aviation; the National Universities Commission records 2023. It was created to meet the need for education that drives technological and economic development in Africa, and to close the gap between graduates' skills and what the aviation industry needs.
368.a: AAAU offers degrees in aeronautical engineering, aviation business and meteorology.
368.c: It is located in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

374.h: The Federal University of Education, Zaria (FUEZ) was created from the former Federal College of Education, Zaria, one of several federal colleges of education upgraded to universities of education. The National Universities Commission records the conversion in 2023. The university has stopped admitting students to the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE); current NCE students will complete their programmes, and new students enter degree programmes.
374.a: The university offers bachelor's degrees in education and related fields, through UTME and direct entry, as well as postgraduate degrees in education.
374.c: It is located at Gyellesu, Zaria, Kaduna State.

378.h: The Federal University of Allied Health Sciences, Enugu (FUAHSE) was founded in 2024 to strengthen Nigeria's health workforce by training allied health professionals and encouraging innovation in health services.
378.a: The university offers degrees in allied health disciplines, the professions that work alongside doctors and nurses. It hosts an international conference, AHiAISE, in partnership with the University of Chichester's Centre for Future Technologies in the United Kingdom and an IEEE skills hub.
378.c: It is located in Enugu, Enugu State.

381.h: The Federal University of Education, Kontagora (FUEK) began in September 1978 as a Federal Advanced Teachers College, set up under the military government of General Olusegun Obasanjo. It was first affiliated to the University of Ilorin, became an autonomous Federal College of Education in 1987 under the National Commission for Colleges of Education, and was later upgraded to a university; the National Universities Commission records 2023.
381.a: The university focuses on teacher education and research into education.
381.c: It is located in Kontagora, Niger State.

384.h: The Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia (FUASK) was established by an Act of the National Assembly in 2025, after President Bola Tinubu signed the bill into law. It took over the buildings of NOK University, a private university that the Federal Government acquired in 2024.
384.a: As a university of applied sciences, it aims to give graduates practical skills for innovation and problem-solving. A College of Medicine is planned near the Federal Medical Centre.
384.c: It is in Kachia town, southern Kaduna State, about 110 kilometres from Kaduna and 90 kilometres from Kafanchan.
